Vice President of Operations
Denver, CO
Hybrid
$210K – $250K • Offers Equity • Offers Bonus
Quindar builds software to manage satellites like servers. We are seeking a Vice President of Operations to build the operating system, organizational infrastructure, and business processes that turn company strategy into execution as we scale across commercial and government markets.
This leader owns business operations, strategy and performance, facilities, and General & Administrative functions. Beyond running the operating cadence, the role connects corporate strategy, resource allocation, and cross-functional execution so that Quindar consistently makes the right investments and turns them into business outcomes. The role holds the authority to resolve cross-functional prioritization conflicts at the leadership level, with clear and intentional escalation to the CEO, while functional leaders retain accountability for their results and authority over their teams.
Facilities, Business Operations, and the G&A team report to this role, with their leaders responsible for day-to-day execution. This is a hands-on executive role for someone who can build a function, develop its leaders, and drive execution across the company.

Company Execution and Performance Management
• Translate company strategy into company OKRs and functional commitments with accountable owners, deadlines, dependencies, and approved resources.
• Agree with each functional leader on a small set of meaningful KPIs with clear definitions, source data, targets, and reporting frequency, and maintain a consolidated performance dashboard across Sales, Product, Engineering, Programs, Finance, People and Brand, and Operations.
• Design and run the company operating model: quarterly planning, leadership reviews, decision tracking, and follow-up, with a visible record of commitments delivered, missed, corrected, and rescoped.
• Design and implement a company-wide model for cross-functional prioritization and decision-making at the leadership level, including decision rights and escalation paths, aligned with and actively reinforced by the CEO.
• Use the operating data to drive decisions and corrective actions, resolve cross-functional dependencies, and escalate decisions that put company goals at risk.
• Partner with functional leaders and the VP of Finance to align workforce capacity, hiring plans, facilities, and budgets with company priorities.

Corporate Strategy and Go-to-Market
• Help shape corporate strategy with the CEO and leadership team, including evaluating markets and opportunities, defining investment requirements, and translating strategic choices into resourced plans.
• Lead the cross-functional planning and execution of GTM priorities in partnership with the CEO, who leads Sales & Marketing: align Product, Engineering, Programs, and Operations behind revenue priorities and ensure the organization is resourced to deliver them.
• Lead the evaluation and incubation of new business opportunities, including, but not limited to,Operations as a Service (OaaS). For OaaS, lead the initial cross-functional effort to take the offering from concept toward launch, including the business model, service definition and commercial terms, investment requirements, and operational readiness.
• Ensure new services, markets, and programs are integrated into company planning, performance management, and compliance from the outset.

AI-Enabled Business Operations
• Lead the AI Business Operations team to build and deploy workflows that reduce manual coordination and increase output across Quindar, with measurable reductions in hands-on processing time and sustained adoption.
• Identify and baseline the highest-value workflows across functions, prioritizing those that remove coordination overhead between Product, Engineering, Programs, Sales, and Marketing (for example, specifications to engineering tickets, user documentation, marketing materials, and proposal development).
• Build internal knowledge infrastructure, such as a company data warehouse of product knowledge, engineering designs, documentation, and marketing and proposal content, that any role can query or use to create collateral through an agentic interface.
• Implement appropriate access controls, source traceability, and compliance requirements, including CUI handling, before any workflow handling sensitive or consequential outputs enters production use.

Facilities and Classified Readiness
• Own facilities planning, buildouts, workplace operations, vendor management, and procurement across all unclassified and classified spaces.
• Maintain an integrated master schedule covering construction, procurement, vendors, budget, and readiness for each space, with a defined risk and impact scale, reviewed regularly with the CEO.
• Deliver the facilities infrastructure needed for classified readiness, completing facilities work ahead of accreditation target dates and obtaining Security’s written acceptance against an agreed readiness checklist.
• Partner with Security, IT, Contracts, and program leadership so that facilities, policies, training, and records support classified program and audit requirements. Security retains accreditation responsibility.

General and Administrative Operations
• Lead legal operations, and corporate administrative services through internal teams and outside partners.
• Manage outside counsel and coordinate corporate legal matters, employment matters, contract review, and company policies.
• Own cap table and stock option administration in partnership with Finance and legal counsel, and maintain corporate records and board and stockholder approval workflows with the CEO and counsel.
• Own the administrative infrastructure required to pursue and support government business, including SAM.gov registration, applicable NSTXL and consortium memberships, JCP certification/DD Form 2345, and a centralized calendar of registrations, renewals, and reporting obligations.
• Oversee export compliance program administration, including applicable ITAR/EAR processes, working with qualified counsel and designated compliance personnel.
• Coordinate corporate insurance, business continuity planning, corporate overhead efficiency, and company-wide operational risk management.

Fundraising and Finance Partnership
• Lead operational, legal, people, and corporate diligence readiness for fundraising alongside the VP of Finance, including an organized data room and timely, accurate responses to investor requests.
• Support board materials and investor reporting with company operating metrics, organizational plans, and progress against strategic priorities.
• Partner with Finance on operating plans, overhead budgets, and the investments needed to support the next stage of growth and new business lines.

Qualifications
• Experience leading operations at a growing technology company, with exposure to government contracting or another regulated market.
• Demonstrated success building teams, systems, and operating processes through a significant stage of organizational growth.
• Experience contributing to corporate strategy and leading cross-functional GTM or new-business initiatives from concept to launch, with a bias toward revenue and business outcomes.
• Experience across facilities, legal operations, compliance, or business operations.
• A hands-on track record of using AI, technology, and automation to improve operational efficiency.
• Familiarity with venture-backed company governance, equity administration, and fundraising diligence.
• Ability to turn ambiguous priorities into clear plans, coordinate executive peers, and hold teams accountable for commitments.
• Strong judgment about when to act directly, delegate, escalate, or engage specialist expertise.

What Success Looks Like
• Company strategy is reflected in OKRs, KPIs, and commitments with clear owners, and leaders run the business from a trusted, shared dashboard.
• Cross-functional prioritization decisions are made quickly and consistently at the leadership level, with less day-to-day intervention from the CEO.
• GTM priorities and new services such as OaaS move from strategy to resourced, cross-functionally executed plans with measurable revenue impact.
• AI-enabled workflows are in production across functions, materially reducing manual coordination while meeting access-control and compliance requirements.
• Facilities for classified operations are delivered on schedule and accepted by Security.
• Organizational structures, career frameworks, equity programs, and scaling processes are ready ahead of growth to 150+ employees.
• Required registrations, compliance obligations, and corporate and equity records remain current and diligence-ready.

Security Clearance Eligibility Requirement
Due to U.S. Government contractual requirements, this position requires eligibility for a U.S. Government security clearance. U.S. citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance; therefore, candidates for this position must be U.S. citizens. An active clearance is not required at the time of hire but is preferred and may be required in the future based on program needs.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS

- To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here .

Why you'll love working at Quindar

- We work in a cutting edge industry and you will get the opportunity to be part of a small team with a large direct impact on the success of our customers’ space missions!

- We take work life balance very seriously. We require employees to take 15 days off but provide unlimited PTO and follow most US federal government holidays.

- Mental health is just as important as physical so we provide quarterly health & wellness benefits.

- Comprehensive health insurance for you and your family with 100% coverage for employees.

- We encourage employees to save for retirement and provide 4% 401(k) matching.

- Each quarter we have a 4-day company offsite. Previous locations include San Francisco, Nashville, Denver, Santa Fe, New Orleans, San Diego, Bozeman, and New York City.

- Our culture and company is evolving. You will be key in creating the next major or minor version!

ARS Pharmaceuticals is a fast-growing, innovative company dedicated to transforming the treatment of severe allergic reactions with neffy® , the first and only FDA-approved needle-free epinephrine product. If you’re motivated to make a meaningful impact, this is your opportunity to join a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and inclusive culture.

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Manager / Sr. Manager, Technical Operations will play a key role in executing Technical Operations programs that support the continued development and commercial supply of neffy™. The successful candidate will combine strong technical judgment, project management, and external partner leadership in a highly collaborative environment.

Working closely with internal stakeholders and CMOs, this role provides technical and operational leadership across the ARS outsourced manufacturing network. Responsibilities include leading Technical Operations projects, supporting formulation and process development, technology transfer, GMP manufacturing activities, and resolution of technical and operational issues. The position ensures project scope, timelines, deliverables, responsibilities, and budgets remain aligned while proactively identifying and escalating risks to support compliant, reliable, and on-time product supply.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

- Manage cross-functional Technical Operations projects and day-to-day technical and operational interactions with assigned external partners, including scope, timelines, deliverables, responsibilities, budgets, risks, key milestones, project meetings, action tracking, scopes of work, proposals, change orders, and CMO/vendor performance metrics and KPIs (e.g., service, quality, delivery, capacity, and right-first-time).

- Serve as a Technical Operations point of contact for assigned external manufacturing partners and work closely with CMOs and internal stakeholders to ensure execution against agreed project plans and supply requirements.

- Provide technical oversight of formulation and process development, scale-up, technology transfer, process characterization, process validation/PPQ, and continued process verification activities, as applicable.

- Plan and support clinical and commercial manufacturing campaigns in coordination with CMOs, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and other internal functions; provide on-site/person-in-plant support for key manufacturing activities as needed.

- Review manufacturing and process documentation, including master and executed batch records, protocols, reports, process performance data, vendor change controls, investigations, and annual/product reviews, for technical accuracy and process performance.

- Lead or support technical assessment and resolution of manufacturing deviations, out-of-specification or atypical results, and other process issues; contribute to root-cause analysis and appropriate corrective and preventive actions in partnership with Quality Assurance.

- Assess proposed manufacturing and process changes for technical impact and support cross-functional evaluation of quality, supply, and regulatory implications.

- Monitor and trend manufacturing and process performance data to identify emerging risks, process drift, and opportunities for continuous improvement and operational excellence.

- Support vendor selection, onboarding, and qualification activities in collaboration with Quality Assurance, Supply Chain, Procurement, and other stakeholders.

- Communicate project status, technical risks, manufacturing issues, and recommend actions clearly to Technical Operations leadership and cross-functional stakeholders; escalate significant issues to appropriate decision-makers.

- Support preparation and review of CMC information for regulatory submissions and responses to health authority questions, as required.

- Support Technical Operations process improvement, business continuity, capacity planning, and other strategic operational initiatives as assigned.

- Support commercial supply operations managed within Technical Operations, including coordination with third-party logistics (3PL) providers, distribution partners, and external manufacturing/packaging partners to maintain reliable product supply.

- Support product serialization activities, including EPCIS data exchange and operational compliance with applicable Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA) requirements, working with packaging, distribution, Quality Assurance, and other partners as appropriate.

- Support clinical supply activities, including coordination with Clinical Operations and external vendors for clinical packaging, labeling, distribution, inventory/expiry management, and Interactive Response Technology/Interactive Web Response System (IRT/IWRS) activities, as applicable.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

- Strong working knowledge of current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP), pharmaceutical manufacturing operations, and applicable quality systems and regulatory expectations.

- Demonstrated technical understanding of formulation, manufacturing processes, scale-up, technology transfer, process validation, and process performance sufficient to critically evaluate CMO data and recommendations, work effectively in cross-functional technical teams, and hold external partners accountable to commitments.

- Strong project and vendor management skills, with demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, timelines, deliverables, and external partners in a fast-paced environment.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate complex manufacturing or process issues, develop recommendations, and communicate the rationale for action.

- Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills with the ability to communicate effectively across functions and organizational levels, including senior management and external partners.

- Well-organized, detail-oriented, and able to identify and escalate risks while maintaining focus on execution and business priorities.

- Proficiency with Microsoft Office and project/reporting tools; experience with project management, continuous improvement, or operational excellence methodologies is a plus.

- Working knowledge of commercial and clinical supply operations relevant to Technical Operations, including 3PL interfaces, serialization/EPCIS and DSCSA requirements, and clinical IRT/IWRS processes; direct experience in one or more of these areas is preferred.

- Must be able to travel domestically and internationally up to approximately 20% to support external manufacturing partners and key project activities.

- Bachelor’s degree in pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry, chemical engineering, engineering, or a related scientific/technical discipline; an advanced degree is a plus. An acceptable combination of education and relevant experience will also be considered.

- Minimum of 5 years of relevant pharmaceutical/biotechnology experience in Technical Operations, manufacturing, process/formulation development, CMC, supply chain, or a related function.

- Experience working with external CMOs/CDMOs and supporting GMP clinical and/or commercial manufacturing is strongly preferred.

- Experience with drug-device combination products, nasal/inhalation products, sterile manufacturing, commercial product launch, or PPQ is preferred.

- Experience reviewing manufacturing batch records and process documentation and supporting technical investigations, change controls, and regulatory CMC activities is preferred.

- Experience supporting commercial distribution/3PL operations, serialization/EPCIS and DSCSA compliance, and/or clinical supply and IRT/IWRS activities is preferred.

About the University

Established in 1965, Metropolitan State University ( MSU Denver ) was founded to serve students who were underrepresented in higher education whose life paths and experiences did not fit the traditional mold. Sixty years later, the University continues to serve over 16,000 of Colorado’s extraordinary and diverse students, providing them with the foundation on which to build their unique aspirations. As the third largest public institution of higher education in Colorado, MSU Denver is a model university for today’s college students.

Proud of its federal designation as a Hispanic-Serving Institution that also offers graduate programs (gHSI) and the only Seal of Excelencia certified institution in Colorado, the University serves the most diverse undergraduate student population in the state, as well as the most first-generation students. Through affordable, flexible, and holistic education, MSU Denver helps students build essential skills grounded in a multicultural and global perspective that lead to undergraduate and graduate degrees, and career and life success.

At MSU Denver, we are committed to our CADRE values: Community, Access, Diversity, Respect, and Excellence. We strive to create a supportive and inclusive environment where all community members are valued and belong. Our dedication to breaking down barriers to education, fostering open dialogue, and promoting world-class scholarship ensures that we provide exceptional services and innovative learning opportunities for our students, faculty, and staff.

Position Summary

MSU Denver seeks a Director to lead the Advanced Manufacturing Sciences Institute ( AMSI ) and advance its development into a sustainable, impactful program. The Director manages all AMSI activities including the Industry 4.0 Center of Excellence which serves Colorado manufacturers through technology demonstrations, training, micro-credentials, and sponsored partnerships. The Director is the primary liaison and point of contact for all industry partners. The Director develops and maintains the Advanced Manufacturing Sciences academic programs in collaboration with various academic departments.

The Director builds integrated pathways for both degree-seeking students and non-degree learners. These pathways connect credentials, work-based learning, undergraduate and graduate programs, and lifelong learning. The Director also makes AMSI a hub for interdisciplinary collaboration within CACED and across the University. Through AMSI, the Director connects academic programs, faculty, students, industry partners, and community organizations around shared learning, applied research, workforce development, and emerging opportunities.

A high priority for the Director is to develop a long-term model that allows AMSI to sustain and grow its programs and activities beyond short-term or one-time funding. The incoming Director will build appropriate revenue-generating activities to support students, programs, equipment, and future growth.

Responsibilities

Institute Strategy

- Set and carry out AMSI’s mission, vision, and annual plan consistent with the strategy, budgets, goals, and policies of CACED and the University.

- Advance industry-relevant technologies, practices, and partnerships that prepare students to contribute from their first day on the job and that address manufacturing workforce gaps.

- Maintain an active Advisory Board and keep it informed through an outcomes dashboard that tracks sponsors, student credit hours, enrollments, non-degree learners served, placements, revenue by source, and other appropriate data.

Institute Sustainability

- Develop a long-term sustainability model and a multi-year business plan that sets out AMSI’s costs, funding sources, and revenue sources; update the plan each year.

- Build a diversified funding base that combines earned revenue, industry partnerships and sponsorships, philanthropy, and public and private grants.

- Develop appropriate revenue-generating activities that are consistent with the University’s mission and strategic plan.

- Oversee fee-based manufacturing services offered by AMSI.

- Pursue grants and other funding that build lasting capacity and plan how successful grant-funded programs and positions will continue after the award ends.

- Partner with the Office of Sponsored Research and Projects and Advancement on identifying and applying for grants, gifts, corporate sponsorships, equipment and donations.

Integrated Learning Pathways

- Work with faculty and academic departments to identify where micro-credentials, industry-recognized credentials, and competency-based training can be included in academic certificates and degrees consistent with University curriculum and credit policies.

- Expand work-based learning with manufacturing employers including internships, apprenticeships, industry-sponsored capstones, and applied projects.

- Strengthen the path from AMS undergraduate programs into graduate study and 4+1 programs.

- Create upskilling and reskilling training opportunities for incumbent workers and adult learners that offer clear entry points into credit-bearing programs.

- Establish transfer and articulation agreements with community colleges and other educational partners.

Interdisciplinary Collaboration

- Bring faculty and students from CACED’s aerospace, computing, engineering, and design programs, and from other appropriate academic programs, together with industry partners on sponsored projects, capstones, applied research, and grant proposals.

- Open AMSI’s labs, equipment, and industry relationships to academic programs across the University for teaching and applied research opportunities.

- Host and participate in convenings and working groups that bring faculty, students, industry partners, and community organizations together on workforce development and emerging technologies.

Industry 4.0 Center of Excellence

- Lead and grow the COE’s fee-for-service and manufacturing services programs through technology demonstrations, corporate training (standard and custom), micro-credentials and certificates, applied research and development, capstone sponsorships, and selective lab and equipment access.

- Draw on manufacturing networks including CAMA, WiM, Manufacturer’s Edge, and MWAMA, and on state and federal funding opportunities, to convene industry partners, launch programs, and generate applied industry projects.

- Standardize scoping, intellectual property, safety, and performance-metric templates for company projects.

Academic Programs

- Develop and maintain the AMS academic programs with faculty and department leaders and keep curricula current with industry needs through regular input from industry partners.

- Oversee student recruitment, retention, and job placement goals and activities.

- Coordinate internship placements, serve as internship advisor, and manage internship evaluations and reporting.

Laboratory Operations

- Oversee AMSI labs and testbeds for safe, scheduled use by multiple academic programs and expand their use for industry collaboration and applied research.

- Plan equipment maintenance, upgrades, and replacement so that AMSI’s technology stays current with industry practice.

Administration

- Supervise, evaluate, and develop AMSI staff and direct their work on the Institute’s priorities in lab operations, business operations, workforce development initiatives, student recruitment and retention, and marketing and communications.

- Prepare annual reports, budget plans, and periodic reviews and maintain sound financial management and risk controls.

- Manage memoranda of understanding and other agreements with academic units and external partners.

Position Competencies

- Champions CADRE values-based leadership and creates a positive workplace culture, by setting expectations, eliciting feedback and coaching across departments, ensuring accountability and excelling in conflict management

- Aligns operations across teams by optimizing resources, maintaining compliance, and empowering leaders to deliver consistent, measurable outcomes

- Translates University strategy into coordinated action by guiding decision-making, prioritizing initiatives, and adjusting plans to drive long-term progress

- Builds cross-functional partnerships, sharing information widely and facilitating dialogue to break down silos and advance University goals

- Creates a positive workplace culture of belonging by embedding equitable leadership and talent processes, fostering feedback and holding leaders accountable

- Drives innovation by aligning initiatives to University priorities, anticipating change, and empowering leaders to implement sustainable improvements

Required Qualifications

- Master’s degree from an accredited institution or an equivalent combination of education and experience

- Working knowledge of advanced manufacturing technologies and the workforce needs of manufacturing employers

- Familiarity with Colorado’s manufacturing employers, industry associations, and workforce funding programs

- Experience supervising staff and managing budgets that draw on multiple funding sources, such as grants, contracts, gifts, or earned revenue

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience building credential programs, apprenticeships, or other work-based learning that connects to degree programs

- A record of leading interdisciplinary initiatives with faculty and partners from multiple disciplines or organizations

- Experience securing state, federal, or foundation grants, and sustaining programs after grant funding ends

- Industry experience in manufacturing, aerospace, or a related sector

- Experience in higher education with diverse, urban student populations

We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every preferred qualification. We are most interested in finding the candidate who will best contribute to the AMSI Institute, our mission, and the University.

Schedule Information

- Full time, 40 hrs/wk

- Exempt

- Days of the Week: Monday - Friday, during regular University business hours that typically range between 8:00 am - 5:00 pm

- Evenings and Weekend Work: As needed for industry events, University events, meetings, and other program activities

- Schedule: Primarily in person on campus with some flexibility for remote work depending upon program needs and supervisor approval

- Travel: Local travel as needed for industry partnerships, employer engagement, and related activities, with occasional travel for conferences or professional development

Salary for Announcement

Under Colorado law, MSU Denver is required to provide a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role and should not offer a salary outside of the range posted in this job announcement. This range takes into account a variety of factors including but not limited to experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, analysis of internal equity, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be offered a salary at or near the top of the range for a position. Salary offers are determined based on final candidate qualifications and experience.

The anticipated hiring range that the university reasonably expects to pay for this position is $115,000 - $130,000.

This position is paid monthly and is eligible for MSU Denver benefits .

The Problem

Severe mental illness affects over 15 million adults in the United States. Schizophrenia. Schizoaffective disorder. Bipolar I. Treatment-resistant depression. These are the conditions the rest of healthcare has systematically failed to build for.

What makes this problem different from most of healthcare is that the tools to solve it do not exist. The clinical protocols, the measurement science, the precision medicine, the technology to deliver coordinated longitudinal outpatient care for this population. None of it has been built. This is a frontier problem, and it requires frontier science and care delivery to solve.

We are developing all of it. The care, the science, the technology.

Who We Are

Amae Health is a Series B, venture-backed Public Benefit Corporation delivering specialty outpatient care for people with severe mental illness through high-acuity, in-person clinics nationwide.

Our integrated model brings psychiatry, therapy, primary care, dietitians, and community support together under one roof. Leading health systems—including New York-Presbyterian, Cedars-Sinai, Mass General Brigham, Novant Health, and CommonSpirit —collaborate with us to expand this level of care.

Alongside care delivery, we are building the science and technology the field has long lacked—proprietary clinical protocols, novel measurement, and an AI-driven data platform designed for severe mental illness.

The impact: fewer hospitalizations, greater stability, and more people living meaningful lives in their communities.

The Team

We are clinicians, operators, technologists, and scientists who chose Amae because the problem is hard and the stakes are real. We are not interested in incremental improvements to a broken system—we are redefining it.
